title: Interpreting Classical Readability Formulae as Surprisal
abstract: arXiv:2611.01359v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Surprisal correlates closely with reading time and is widely used in the cognitive science of reading as a measure of processing difficulty. Classical readability formulae such as the Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level, which scores a text by the US school grade expected to read it, are the most widely used practical measures of text difficulty, but their coefficients are unitless regression constants and have never been related to surprisal. We theoretically show that these coefficients can be interpreted as surprisal: every formula of the classical additive shape is a sum of per-word and per-sentence cross-entropies under a memoryless model, and once that model is tied to the language through Zipf's law and the formula is read as its linearisation at a reference text, each coefficient factorises into a scale in grades per nat, a Zipf slope and a reference sentence length. translated_title: 将经典可读性公式解释为惊讶度
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.01359v1 公告类型：新 摘要：惊讶度与阅读时间密切相关，被广泛用作阅读认知科学中衡量加工难度的指标。诸如Flesch-Kincaid年级水平这类经典可读性公式——它按照预期读者所需达到的美国学校年级为文本评分——是实际中使用最广泛的文本难度度量方法，但其系数是无量纲的回归常数，从未与惊讶度建立起联系。我们从理论上证明，这些系数可以被解释为惊讶度：每一类具有经典加法形式的公式，都是在无记忆模型下逐词交叉熵与逐句交叉熵之和；一旦该模型通过Zipf定律与语言绑定，且该公式被理解为其在某个参考文本处的线性化，则每个系数便可以分解为一个以“每nat年级数”为单位的尺度因子、一个Zipf斜率以及一个参考句子长度。由此，年级本身成为了一个惊讶度意义上的量。由于该公式……
tldr: 该论文首次从理论上证明，Flesch-Kincaid等经典可读性公式的系数可被解释为惊讶度——在无记忆模型下，这类公式等价于逐词与逐句交叉熵之和，借助Zipf定律并作为参考文本处的线性化，每个系数可分解为每nat年级数尺度、Zipf斜率和参考句子长度，从而使“年级”成为惊讶度的一个量。
en_tdlr: This paper theoretically shows that the coefficients of classical readability formulae such as Flesch-Kincaid can be interpreted as surprisal: under a memoryless model, these additive formulae are sums of per-word and per-sentence cross-entropies, and once tied to language through Zipf's law and read as a linearization at a reference text, each coefficient factorizes into a scale in grades per nat, a Zipf slope, and a reference sentence length, making a grade a quantity in surprisal.
